newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Dead Sea in talks to acquire Czech firm.
newsitem.headline: Dead Sea in talks to acquire Czech firm.

text.p: Israel's Dead Sea Works (DSW) and its sister company Dead Sea Bromine Group are in negotiations to acquire a majority holding in a Czech producer of fine chemicals, DSW President Uri Ben-Noon said on Tuesday.
"The Czech company has big potential for us," he told Reuters.

Ben-Noon said the Czech company was a leading producer of fine chemicals for the pharmaceuticals industry, but he refused to provide further details about it. He indicated the talks were in an advanced stage.

If the sale goes through, the Czech company will produce fine chemicals developed by Bromine as well as its current product line. The Israeli companies view fine chemicals as one of the areas they want to move into as part of their diversification strategy.

The two Israeli companies are subsidiaries of Israel Chemicals Ltd. DSW, which produces potash and other chemicals from the Dead Sea, had revenues of 828 million shekels in the first nine months of 1996, while Bromine had revenues of 1.12 billion shekels.
